headline: HOGS BREAK HARD; CATTLE HOLD; CHS DROPS $700M ON CRUSH
lead: Lean hogs dropped 2.2% to $79.72, their sharpest single-session decline in weeks, while cattle ran the other way: live at $222.20, feeders at $343.70, both posting solid gains on strong cash and technicals. Beans recovered a nickel to $13.00, corn slipped a penny and a half.
teaser: Hogs broke hard, cattle ran, and CHS just committed $700M to soy crush in Wisconsin.

one_number.unit: CHS soybean crush plant, Evansville WI
one_number.context: CHS announced a new 700-million-dollar crush facility in Wisconsin today. That is a long-term structural demand commitment to US soybeans that the board has not priced yet.

yesterdays_call.note: Miss. Beans ticked up a nickel to $13.00 instead of breaking lower; the line held and the thesis stays alive but unconfirmed.
yesterdays_call.call_line: Called soybeans down toward $12.8 ($12.945 when the call was made). It closed at $13.0025.

action: Fall calves unpriced: feeders at $343.70 and rising; a close above $345.00 is the signal to lock at least the first third.

sections.title: CATTLE RUN; HOGS BREAK
sections.body: - Live cattle at **$222.20** and feeders at $343.70 extended gains on strong cash trade, with AgWeb flagging fund interest returning to the long side after weeks of sitting out.
sections.so_what: Cattle and feeders are running on supply tightness; hogs are on their own.

sections.title: BEANS RECOVER; CORN FLAT
sections.body:
- Soybeans at **$13.00** recovered a nickel after yesterday's crack; corn flat.
- The CHS crush plant (see today's One Number) tells you commercial money is betting on US soybean supply for years out.
sections.so_what: Beans steadied but $13.00 is not a clean recovery; needs a close above.

sections.title: CRUDE HOLDS $102; SAUDI PIPELINE OUT WEEKS
sections.body: - WTI at **$102.57** barely moved, but Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline -- hit by drone strikes earlier this month -- could take weeks to repair, cutting regional crude flows.
sections.so_what: Two supply disruptions running simultaneously; harvest diesel costs are not easing before October.

outside_the_pit.title: Senate Ag Committee Meets Wednesday on Farm Bill
outside_the_pit.body: The Senate Ag Committee reconvenes Wednesday as McConnell returns, with the Sep 30 extension deadline closing fast after the Aug 6 markup failed on party lines.

watch_list.desc: Senate Ag Committee farm bill meeting; a deal before Sep 30 or another extension. Watch for year-round E15 language.
Weekly export sales; beans under 300K MT keeps the $13.00 recovery thin and fund-driven, not demand-driven.
Crop Progress; corn harvest pace above 10% sets harvest-pressure tone, below 5% means weather is the story.

daily_quote.text: It's not the will to win that matters — everyone has that. It's the will to prepare to win that matters.
